newsitem.title: DUBAI: Robust Indian demand bolsters Dubai gold market.
newsitem.headline: Robust Indian demand bolsters Dubai gold market.

text.p: Strong Indian demand for gold buoyed the Dubai market in the week to Sunday, but traders said local retail interest had fallen sharply in the past few weeks since the end of a government-sponsored shopping promotion.
They said prices in Dubai had increased in line with a sharp rise in international bullion late in the week, spurred by a fall in the dollar and a COMEX options expiry.

"The local demand is a little down. There has been no recovery since the end of the Dubai shopping festival, but Indian demand for both gold and silver is great," said one dealer dominant in the Dubai-India precious metals trade.
The wedding season in India, which winds down in the next month or so, continues to fan demand.
But traders forecast a slowdown in the next three months.

"The seasonal demand will continue just until the first week of June. The monsoon usually starts in the second week," said one. "The marriage season will be over and there are no major festivals for the next three months," he added.
Mirroring a jump of more than seven dollars an ounce in world gold prices in the week, the price of Dubai's benchmark ten tola bar rose to 4,810 dirhams ($1,310) from 4,705 dirhams a week earlier.
The ten tola bar contains 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold.
On the international spot market, gold was quoted late Saturday at $347.80/$348.30 an ounce versus $340.00/50 a week earlier.

Despite the slowdown in local retail trade since the month-long Dubai shopping promotion closed at end-April, traders took heart from latest data from the World Gold Council, a producer group which aims to promote usage of the metal.

WGC figures showed the emirate more than doubled imports of the precious metal to almost 155 tonnes in the first three months of the year, compared with the same previous year period, thanks mainly to robust Indian demand and weak world prices.

Dubai is the main distribution hub for India, the world's largest consumer of the yellow metal. Some 85 percent of the 154.909 tonnes imported into Dubai in the first quarter was re-exported to India, the WGC said.
Dubai traders have said they expect total gold imports this year of well over 400 tonnes compared to imports of 350 tonnes last year if this year's monsoon yields a good harvest.
